info.title: Unikraft Cloud Sandbox Plugin API
info.description:
This specification describes the Sandbox plugin API, a control API exposed by
a sandbox instance running on Unikraft Cloud. It provides two services: the
management of shell commands running inside the sandbox, and reading and
writing files in the sandbox filesystem.

Every operation declares a `default` response: the standard response
envelope, which carries the outcome of the request in `status`, the
human-readable reason for a failure in `message` and the HTTP status code in
`errors`. The HTTP status code itself distinguishes success from failure; the
status codes an operation can return are documented on the operation. The two
endpoints which stream bytes rather than JSON (the raw command log and the
raw file download) return their payload verbatim, unenveloped.

`GET /commands/{uuid}/ws` also declares `101`: it upgrades to a WebSocket
that streams a command's output as it is produced and takes its input,
`eof`, `resize` and `signal` as frames. The frame contract is documented in
the plugin's README.

get.description:
List the UUIDs of all commands, in the order they were started.

This operation is also the plugin's readiness probe: it takes no
parameters, changes nothing, and answers on an empty sandbox, so a client
can call it to establish that the plugin is serving before it sends any
real work. Hence `x-unikraft-plugin-readiness`, which the SDK generators
read to render their readiness helpers against this operation.

default.description: The UUIDs of all known commands.

post.description:
Start a command in the sandbox, and with `req_timeout_s` wait for it, so
that starting, waiting, inspecting and fetching the output take one
request. `500` is returned when the command could not be spawned, and
`400` when `cols` or `rows` are given without `pty` or are zero, when
`req_timeout_s` is not between 0 (exclusive) and 55 seconds, or when
`logs_limit` or `forget` are given without `req_timeout_s`.

default.description: The command that was started, as GET .../{uuid} describes it, plus its output (logs) when req_timeout_s was given.

get.description:
Inspect a command by UUID. `404` is returned, with an empty body, when no
such command exists.

default.description: The command line and exit status of the command.

delete.description:
Forget a command by UUID. `404` is returned, with an empty body, when no
such command exists, and `409` when the command has not finished
executing: commands which are still running cannot be forgotten.

default.description: The outcome of forgetting the command.

delete.description:
Forget the output logs of an existing command, freeing up memory.
The stdin/out/err pipes of running commands will be closed. Idempotent.
`404` is returned, with an empty body, when no such command exists.
With persistence, the log files go first; should neither go (`500`),
nothing is deleted and the logs stay.

default.description: The outcome of forgetting command logs.

get.description:
Fetch the collected output of a command; this changes nothing, releasing
is `POST .../logs/release`. Both streams are base64-encoded; use the raw
log endpoint for binary output. `404` is returned, with an empty body,
when no such command exists. `410` is returned, with an empty body, if the
command's logs have been deleted. `416` is returned, with a message naming
the first byte still available, when an `offset` is below what was
released. With persistence, output past the ceiling is in the log file
while the command runs, read as one stream with memory; unread output
there is bounded (a quarter of the volume, 4 GiB at most, never into its
last quarter), past which the command is held as without a volume.

default.description: The requested parts of the two output streams.

get.description:
Fetch an output stream of a command as raw bytes. A single contiguous
`Range` header is honoured, as described in RFC 9110. Once part of the
stream was released (see `POST .../logs/release`), a request without a `Range` is
answered with `206` and what is still available, or `416` once all of it
was released, and a `Range` into the released part with `416`. A stream
longer than what memory can hold, on a volume while the command runs, is
answered a page of that size at a time, `206` with a `Content-Range`.

parameters.name: Range
parameters.description: A single contiguous byte range, e.g. `bytes=0-1023`.

default.description:
An output stream of a command, returned verbatim and unenveloped. A request
carrying no `Range` header is answered with `200` and the whole stream (or,
once part of it was released, with `206` and what is still available, and
with `416` once all of it was); a
satisfiable `Range` is answered with `206`, the requested bytes and a
`Content-Range` header. `404` is returned when the command or the stream does
not exist, `410` is returned, with an empty body, if the command's logs have been
deleted, and `416` — with a `Content-Range` header reporting the total length —
when the range cannot be satisfied.

Content-Range.description:
The range of bytes returned and the total length of the stream, as
described in RFC 9110. Only present on a partial (`206`) response.

post.description:
Release what the client has of a command's output; a read never does.
`404` is returned, with an empty body, when no such command exists, `410`
if the command's logs have been deleted, and `400` when the body is not
offsets. With persistence, output past the ceiling is in the log file
while the command runs, and a release frees it there too.

default.description: The outcome of releasing the output.

post.description:
Resize a command's terminal; the foreground job is told with SIGWINCH.
`404` is returned, with an empty body, when no such command exists, `400`
when the command has no terminal or the size is zero, and `409` once the
command has finished.

default.description: The outcome of resizing the terminal.

post.description:
Send a signal to a command. `404` is returned, with an empty body, when no
such command exists, and `400` when the signal is not one: a number the
kernel does not have, or a name that is not a signal's.

default.description: The outcome of sending the signal.

post.description:
Feed data into the standard input of a command. `404` is returned, with an
empty body, when no such command exists, `410` if the command's logs have been
deleted, `400` when `data` is not valid base64, `409` when the command has
finished or its standard input is closed (an `eof` alone is still fine),
and `429` when the command has not yet read what it was already given
(its stdin queue holds 8 MiB; on a terminal an `eof` counts as the byte
it types).

default.description: The outcome of feeding the data into standard input.

post.description:
Wait for a command to finish, for up to `timeout_s` seconds, 55 when
absent, which is the most there is. `408` is returned when the time is up
with the command still running, `404`, with an empty body, when no such
command exists, and `400` when `timeout_s` is not between 0 and 55 or the
body does not parse.

default.description: Returned once the command has finished, within the timeout.

post.description:
The old name for `POST .../wait` with a body: the same wait, `408` when
the time is up with the command still running, `404`, with an empty body,
when no such command exists, and `400` when `timeout_s` is not between 0
and 55.

default.description: Returned once the command has finished, within the timeout.

get.description:
Follow a command over a WebSocket: what it has said from the given
offsets on, then everything new as it arrives, then its exit. The socket
also takes the command's input, `eof`, `resize` and `signal` as frames,
as the plugin's README describes. `404` is returned, with an empty body,
when no such command exists, and `400` when the request is not a
WebSocket upgrade or its query does not parse. What the other operations
answer with `410` or `416` is no HTTP status here: a command whose logs
were deleted, or an offset behind what was released (or past the end,
with `release`), gets the upgrade and then a `1008` close.

parameters.name: stdout
parameters.description:
The bytes of standard output the client already has. Omitted, from
where the stream starts: byte 0, or what is still available once some
was released.

parameters.name: release
parameters.description:
Release the offsets the session starts from, then each frame once sent,
as `POST .../logs/release` does. A frame still on its way when the
session drops is gone with it.

101.description:
The switch to a WebSocket that follows a command. Its frames are the
plugin's contract, documented in its README, not this specification's.

post.description:
Create a directory in the sandbox filesystem. `500` is returned when the
directory could not be created.

default.description: The outcome of creating the directory.

post.description:
Read the contents of a file, base64-encoded. `500` is returned when the
file could not be read.

default.description: The base64-encoded contents of the file.

post.description: Download the contents of a file verbatim.

default.description:
The contents of a file, returned verbatim and unenveloped. `404` is returned
when the file does not exist.

post.description:
Upload a file to the sandbox at a given path. A new file will be created at
- if `path` ends with '/' or exists and is a directory: path/filename
- else: path
`400` is returned when `encoding` is not a known encoding or `data` is not
valid base64, and `500` when the file could not be created.

default.description: The outcome of uploading the file.

post.description:
Write data to a file, creating it if it does not exist. `400` is returned
when `encoding` is not a known encoding or `data` is not valid base64, and
`500` when the file could not be written.

default.description: The outcome of writing the file.

CommandLineArgs.description: The command as an argument vector, executed directly without a shell.

CommandLineShell.description: The command line, interpreted by the shell.

CommandLogStream.description: The output stream to read raw bytes from.

stdout.description:
The requested part of the standard output stream, base64-encoded: from
the `offset` asked for, or from `stdout_first` when none was (the same
for `stderr`).

stderr.description: The requested part of the standard error stream, base64-encoded.

stdout_available.description:
The total number of bytes the standard output stream has produced so far,
released ones included: what is still available starts at `stdout_first`.

stderr_available.description: The same for the standard error stream.

stdout_first.description:
The first byte of the standard output stream still available:
everything before it was released. 0 unless something was; kept once
the output is a file, and across a restart.

stderr_first.description: The same for the standard error stream.

CommandLogsData.description: The collected output of a command.

offset.description:
The first byte of the stream to return. Omitted, the stream from where
it starts: byte 0, or what is still available once some was released.
Given, it may not be below what was released: that is a `416`.

limit.description:
The maximum number of bytes to return; omitted, the rest of the stream.
A stream comes whole up to what memory can hold, a little over 18 MiB;
one longer than that, which only a volume allows, is answered in pages of
that size, `limit` or not.

CommandLogsRange.description: The byte range of a single output stream to return.

stdout.description:
Free the standard output stream below this byte: the client has it and
will not ask for it again. A command held at its output ceiling
(`capped`) carries on once there is room. More than there is frees what
there is; no more than was released already does nothing, so a retry is
harmless. Released bytes are gone, from memory and from the log file
where some had spilled to it: a read's `stdout_first` says where what is
left starts, and an `offset` below it is a `416`. Once the command has
exited and its log is a file, a release does nothing: the file is the
archive, and `stdout_first` stays where releases left it while it ran.

stderr.description: The same for the standard error stream.

CommandLogsReleaseRequest.description: What the client has of each output stream, to release.

stdout.description: The part of the standard output stream to return.

stderr.description: The part of the standard error stream to return.

CommandLogsRequest.description:
The (optional) request body limiting which parts of the output streams are
returned. When omitted, both streams are returned in their entirety.

message.description: An optional message providing additional information about the status.

data.description: The response data for this request.

errors.description: A list of errors which may have occurred during the request.

CommandLogsResponse.description:
The response to fetching the output of a command. `404` is returned, with an
empty body, when no command with the given UUID exists. `410` is returned, with an
empty body, if the command's logs have been deleted.

CommandResizeRequest.description: The request to resize a command's terminal.

signal.description:
The signal to send, either as a number or as a name, with or without the
`SIG` prefix, e.g. `15`, `TERM` or `SIGTERM`. `0` sends nothing and only
checks that the command can be signalled. Real-time signals go by number:
where `SIGRTMIN` sits is up to the program's libc (34 on glibc, 35 on
musl), so they have no names here.

CommandSignalRequest.description: The request to send a signal to a command.

data.description: The bytes to feed into standard input, base64-encoded.

eof.description: Whether to close standard input after injecting `data`.

CommandStdinRequest.description: The request to feed data into a command's standard input.

timeout_s.description:
The longest to wait, in seconds; decimals are accepted, `0` only asks.
At most 55, and 55 when absent: a proxy in front cuts a silent request
at about a minute, so a longer wait is a loop on `408`.

CommandWaitRequest.description: The request to wait for a command to finish.

timeout_s.description: The maximum time to wait, in seconds, at most 55. Decimals are accepted.

CommandWaitTimeoutRequest.description: The request to wait for a command to finish, up to a timeout.

message.description: An optional message providing additional information about the status.

data.description: The response data for this request.

errors.description: A list of errors which may have occurred during the request.

EmptyResponse.description:
A response which carries no data of its own. `data` is `null`; the outcome of
the request is the HTTP status code.

FileEncoding.description: The encoding of the data written to a file.

cmdline.description:
The command the command was started with, in the form it was supplied in:
a shell command line, or an argument vector.

cwd.description: The current working directory, if supplied at startup, else null

env.description: Environment variables, if supplied at startup, else null

pty.description: Whether the command runs on a pseudo-terminal.

duration_ms.description:
Milliseconds from start to exit, or to now while the command runs. `null`
for a command restored from a status file written before it was recorded.

exitcode.description:
The exit code of the command. It is `null` while the command is still
running.

capped.description:
Whether the command is held at the output ceiling: the memory for output,
its own share of it (at most 16 MiB) or the sandbox's whole budget across
commands, is full of output nothing has released, so nothing more of it
is read and it blocks in its next write. Releasing some (see
`POST .../logs/release`) lets it carry on. With persistence, output at
the ceiling goes to the log file instead and the command carries on,
which is not `capped`: it is only once the volume's share for unread
output is used up or the volume will not take a spill. Either way `true`
means a release is the way on. `false` once it has finished.

GetCommandData.description: The state of a single command.

message.description: An optional message providing additional information about the status.

data.description: The response data for this request.

errors.description: A list of errors which may have occurred during the request.

GetCommandResponse.description:
The response to inspecting a command. `404` is returned, with an empty body,
when no command with the given UUID exists.

commands.description: The UUIDs of all known commands, in the order they were started.

message.description: An optional message providing additional information about the status.

data.description: The response data for this request.

errors.description: A list of errors which may have occurred during the request.

ListCommandsResponse.description: The response to listing the commands known to the sandbox.

path.description: The absolute path of the directory to create.

parents.description: Whether to create missing parent directories.

MkdirRequest.description: The request to create a directory in the sandbox filesystem.

contents.description: The contents of the file, base64-encoded.

path.description: The absolute path of the file to read.

ReadFileRequest.description: The request to read a file from the sandbox filesystem.

message.description: An optional message providing additional information about the status.

data.description: The response data for this request.

errors.description: A list of errors which may have occurred during the request.

ReadFileResponse.description:
The response to reading a file. `500` is returned when the file could not be
read.

status.description: The HTTP status code of the error.

ResponseError.description: The error response message for an API request.

ResponseStatus.description: The response status of an API request.

cmdline.description:
The command the command was started with, in the form it was supplied in:
a shell command line, or an argument vector.

cwd.description: The current working directory, if supplied at startup, else null

env.description: Environment variables, if supplied at startup, else null

pty.description: Whether the command runs on a pseudo-terminal.

duration_ms.description:
Milliseconds from start to exit, or to now while the command runs. `null`
for a command restored from a status file written before it was recorded.

exitcode.description:
The exit code of the command. It is `null` while the command is still
running.

capped.description:
Whether the command is held at the output ceiling: the memory for output,
its own share of it (at most 16 MiB) or the sandbox's whole budget across
commands, is full of output nothing has released, so nothing more of it
is read and it blocks in its next write. Releasing some (see
`POST .../logs/release`) lets it carry on. With persistence, output at
the ceiling goes to the log file instead and the command carries on,
which is not `capped`: it is only once the volume's share for unread
output is used up or the volume will not take a spill. Either way `true`
means a release is the way on. `false` once it has finished.

logs.description:
Only with `req_timeout_s`: the output, as `GET .../logs` returns it.
Absent if the logs were deleted while the request waited.

RunCommandData.description: The command that was started, as `GET .../{uuid}` describes it.

cmd.description:
The command to run: a command line interpreted by the shell, or an argument
vector executed directly. A bare program name in a vector is looked up in
the `PATH` of `env`, falling back to the sandbox's own `PATH`. `400` is
returned if the vector is empty, the program cannot be resolved or run,
`cwd` is not a directory, an environment variable name is empty or has a
`=` in it, or the request holds what exec will not take (NUL bytes, an
argument list past the kernel's limit).

env.description:
(OPTIONAL) Environment variables: the command's whole environment,
unless the sandbox is configured with `inherit_env`, when they are laid
over the environment the sandbox itself was started with.

pty.description:
(OPTIONAL) Run the command on a pseudo-terminal instead of pipes. Its
output, stdout and stderr merged as a terminal shows them, is served as
`stdout`; input fed to it is echoed by the terminal; an `eof` on stdin
types the terminal's end-of-input character rather than closing anything;
and deleting the logs hangs the terminal up, which ends most commands.
`TERM` is set to `xterm-256color` unless `env` provides one.

cols.description: (OPTIONAL) The terminal's width in columns. Needs `pty`; 80 by default.

rows.description: (OPTIONAL) The terminal's height in rows. Needs `pty`; 24 by default.

stdin.description:
(OPTIONAL) Bytes to feed into standard input before anything else,
base64-encoded, exactly as a `POST .../stdin` right after the start would.

stdin_eof.description:
(OPTIONAL) Whether to close standard input after `stdin` (at once when
there is none). Defaults to `true` when `req_timeout_s` is given, since
nothing can be fed until the request answers, and to `false` otherwise.

req_timeout_s.description:
(OPTIONAL) Block until the command exits or this many seconds have
passed, then answer with the command's state and output (`logs`). More
than 0 and at most 55: a proxy in front cuts a silent request at about a
minute. A timeout is not an error: the answer has `exitcode: null`, the
output so far, and the command keeps running, addressable by UUID as any
other. Absent: answer as soon as the command has started.

logs_limit.description:
(OPTIONAL) With `req_timeout_s`: at most this many bytes of each stream in
the answer, the rest staying at `GET .../logs`. Whole streams by default.

forget.description:
(OPTIONAL) With `req_timeout_s`: forget the command once it has finished,
as `DELETE .../{uuid}` would, so that one request is the whole exchange.
Does nothing on a timeout, when the UUID is still needed, nor when the
answer had to leave output behind short of what was asked (no
`logs_limit`, or one past the bound): a persisted log that spilled past
the ceiling is answered up to what memory could have held (a little
over 18 MiB), and the command then stays for `GET .../logs`,
`stdout_available`/`stderr_available` past what the answer carries
showing it.

RunCommandRequest.description: The request to start a command in the sandbox.

message.description: An optional message providing additional information about the status.

data.description: The response data for this request.

errors.description: A list of errors which may have occurred during the request.

RunCommandResponse.description:
The response to starting a command. `500` is returned when the command could
not be spawned.

path.description: Path where to upload the file.

filename.description: Name of uploaded file; will be used if `path` is a directory.

parents.description: Whether to create parent directories of `path`.

data.description: The data to write, in the given encoding

UploadFileRequest.description: The request to upload a file to the sandbox filesystem.

path.description: The absolute path of the file to write. It is created if missing.

append.description: Whether to append to the file instead of truncating it.

data.description: The data to write, in the given encoding.

WriteFileRequest.description: The request to write a file in the sandbox filesystem.

servers.description: A sandbox running locally, listening on its default port
The sandbox plugin route of an instance running on a Unikraft Cloud metro

metro.description: The metro the instance is running in, e.g. `fra`.

instance.description: The UUID or name of the instance running the sandbox.
